audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Deuteronomy / Devarim divorce, pledge, kidnapping, wage, individual-liability, and gleaning law, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for divorce certificate and remarriage restriction, newlywed exemption, millstone and garment pledges, kidnapping, skin-disease instruction, wage payment, individual responsibility, and gleaning for vulnerable residents.

verses.restored: If a man takes a woman and becomes her husband, and it is that she finds no favor in his eyes because he found in her nakedness/indecency of a thing, and he writes for her a scroll of cutting-off/divorce, puts it in her hand, and sends her from his house,

familiar.text: When a man hath taken a wife, and married her, and it come to pass that she find no favour in his eyes, because he hath found some uncleanness in her: then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house.

modern.text: If a man marries a woman, but she becomes displeasing to him because he finds some indecency in her, he may write her a certificate of divorce, hand it to her, and send her away from his house.

original.text: כִּֽי יִקַּ֥ח אִ֛ישׁ אִשָּׁ֖ה וּבְעָלָ֑הּ וְהָיָ֞ה אִם לֹ֧א תִמְצָא חֵ֣ן בְּעֵינָ֗יו כִּי מָ֤צָא בָהּ֙ עֶרְוַ֣ת דָּבָ֔ר וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּיתֽוֹ

verses.restored: and she goes out from his house and goes and becomes wife of another man,

familiar.text: And when she is departed out of his house, she may go and be another man’s wife.

modern.text: If, after leaving his house, she goes and becomes another man’s wife,

original.text: וְיָצְאָ֖ה מִבֵּית֑וֹ וְהָלְכָ֖ה וְהָיְתָ֥ה לְאִישׁ אַחֵֽר

verses.restored: and latter husband hates her and writes for her a scroll of cutting-off, puts it in her hand, and sends her from his house, or latter husband who took her as wife dies,

familiar.text: And if the latter husband hate her, and write her a bill of divorcement, and giveth it in her hand, and sendeth her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, which took her to be his wife;

modern.text: and the second man hates her, writes her a certificate of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house, or if he dies,

original.text: וּשְׂנֵאָהּ֮ הָאִ֣ישׁ הָאַחֲרוֹן֒ וְכָ֨תַב לָ֜הּ סֵ֤פֶר כְּרִיתֻת֙ וְנָתַ֣ן בְּיָדָ֔הּ וְשִׁלְּחָ֖הּ מִבֵּית֑וֹ א֣וֹ כִ֤י יָמוּת֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הָאַחֲר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר לְקָחָ֥הּ ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: then her first husband who sent her away may not return to take her to become his wife after she has been made unclean, for that is an abomination before YHWH; you shall not cause land to sin that YHWH your Divine gives you as inheritance.

familiar.text: Her former husband, which sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before the LORD: and thou shalt not cause the land to sin, which the LORD thy God giveth thee for an inheritance.

modern.text: then the husband who divorced her first may not remarry her after she has been defiled, for that is an abomination to the LORD. You must not bring sin upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.

original.text: לֹא יוּכַ֣ל בַּעְלָ֣הּ הָרִאשׁ֣וֹן אֲשֶֽׁר שִׁ֠לְּחָהּ לָשׁ֨וּב לְקַחְתָּ֜הּ לִהְי֧וֹת ל֣וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֗ה אַחֲרֵי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֻטַּמָּ֔אָה כִּֽי תוֹעֵבָ֥ה הִ֖וא לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א תַחֲטִיא֙ אֶת הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָֽה

verses.restored: When a man takes a new wife, he shall not go out with host, and no matter shall pass upon him; free he shall be for his house one year, and he shall gladden wife whom he took.

familiar.text: When a man hath taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business: but he shall be free at home one year, and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken.

modern.text: If a man is newly married, he must not be sent to war or be pressed into any duty. For one year he is free to stay at home and bring joy to the wife he has married. Additional Laws

original.text: כִּֽי יִקַּ֥ח אִישׁ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה חֲדָשָׁ֔ה לֹ֤א יֵצֵא֙ בַּצָּבָ֔א וְלֹא יַעֲבֹ֥ר עָלָ֖יו לְכָל דָּבָ֑ר נָקִ֞י יִהְיֶ֤ה לְבֵיתוֹ֙ שָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְשִׂמַּ֖ח אֶת אִשְׁתּ֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר לָקָֽח

verses.restored: One shall not take a handmill or upper millstone as pledge, for he takes a soul/life as pledge.

familiar.text: No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge: for he taketh a man’s life to pledge.

modern.text: Do not take a pair of millstones or even an upper millstone as security for a debt, because that would be taking one’s livelihood as security.

original.text: לֹא יַחֲבֹ֥ל רֵחַ֖יִם וָרָ֑כֶב כִּי נֶ֖פֶשׁ ה֥וּא חֹבֵֽל

verses.restored: If a man is found stealing a soul/person from his brothers, children of Israel, and he treats him as merchandise or sells him, then that thief shall die; so you shall remove evil from your midst.

familiar.text: If a man be found stealing any of his brethren of the children of Israel, and maketh merchandise of him, or selleth him; then that thief shall die; and thou shalt put evil away from among you.

modern.text: If a man is caught kidnapping one of his Israelite brothers, whether he treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die. So you must purge the evil from among you.

original.text: כִּי יִמָּצֵ֣א אִ֗ישׁ גֹּנֵ֨ב נֶ֤פֶשׁ מֵאֶחָיו֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהִתְעַמֶּר בּ֖וֹ וּמְכָר֑וֹ וּמֵת֙ הַגַּנָּ֣ב הַה֔וּא וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: Guard yourself concerning affliction of scale-disease, to keep greatly and do according to all Levitical priests instruct you; as I commanded them, you shall keep to do.

familiar.text: Take heed in the plague of leprosy, that thou observe diligently, and do according to all that the priests the Levites shall teach you: as I commanded them, so ye shall observe to do.

modern.text: In cases of infectious skin diseases, be careful to diligently follow everything the Levitical priests instruct you. Be careful to do as I have commanded them.

original.text: הִשָּׁ֧מֶר בְּנֶֽגַע הַצָּרַ֛עַת לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מְאֹ֖ד וְלַעֲשׂ֑וֹת כְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר יוֹר֨וּ אֶתְכֶ֜ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים הַלְוִיִּ֛ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖ם תִּשְׁמְר֥וּ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת

verses.restored: Remember what YHWH your Divine did to Miriam on way when you came out from Egypt.

familiar.text: Remember what the LORD thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt.

modern.text: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the journey after you came out of Egypt.

original.text: זָכ֕וֹר אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לְמִרְיָ֑ם בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֥ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: When you lend your brother any loan, you shall not enter his house to take his pledge.

familiar.text: When thou dost lend thy brother any thing, thou shalt not go into his house to fetch his pledge.

modern.text: When you lend anything to your neighbor, do not enter his house to collect security.

original.text: כִּֽי תַשֶּׁ֥ה בְרֵֽעֲךָ מַשַּׁ֣את מְא֑וּמָה לֹא תָבֹ֥א אֶל בֵּית֖וֹ לַעֲבֹ֥ט עֲבֹטֽוֹ

verses.restored: Outside you shall stand, and man to whom you lend shall bring pledge out to you.

familiar.text: Thou shalt stand abroad, and the man to whom thou dost lend shall bring out the pledge abroad unto thee.

modern.text: You are to stand outside while the man to whom you are lending brings the security out to you.

original.text: בַּח֖וּץ תַּעֲמֹ֑ד וְהָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ נֹשֶׁ֣ה ב֔וֹ יוֹצִ֥יא אֵלֶ֛יךָ אֶֽת הַעֲב֖וֹט הַחֽוּצָה

verses.restored: If he is poor man, you shall not lie down with his pledge.

familiar.text: And if the man be poor, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge:

modern.text: If he is a poor man, you must not go to sleep with the security in your possession;

original.text: וְאִם אִ֥ישׁ עָנִ֖י ה֑וּא לֹ֥א תִשְׁכַּ֖ב בַּעֲבֹטֽוֹ

verses.restored: You shall surely return pledge to him when sun goes down, so he may lie in his garment and bless you; and it shall be righteousness for you before YHWH your Divine.

familiar.text: In any case thou shalt deliver him the pledge again when the sun goeth down, that he may sleep in his own raiment, and bless thee: and it shall be righteousness unto thee before the LORD thy God.

modern.text: be sure to return it to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in his own cloak and bless you, and this will be credited to you as righteousness before the LORD your God.

original.text: הָשֵׁב֩ תָּשִׁ֨יב ל֤וֹ אֶֽת הַעֲבוֹט֙ כְּבֹ֣א הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ וְשָׁכַ֥ב בְּשַׂלְמָת֖וֹ וּבֵֽרֲכֶ֑ךָּ וּלְךָ֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה צְדָקָ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: You shall not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy, from your brothers or from your sojourner who is in your land within your gates.

familiar.text: Thou shalt not oppress an hired servant that is poor and needy, whether he be of thy brethren, or of thy strangers that are in thy land within thy gates:

modern.text: Do not oppress a hired hand who is poor and needy, whether he is a brother or a foreigner residing in one of your towns.

original.text: לֹא תַעֲשֹׁ֥ק שָׂכִ֖יר עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְי֑וֹן מֵאַחֶ֕יךָ א֧וֹ מִגֵּרְךָ֛ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּאַרְצְךָ֖ בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: In his day you shall give his wage, and sun shall not go down upon it, for he is poor and sets his soul/life upon it; lest he cry against you to YHWH and sin/misalignment be in you.

familiar.text: At his day thou shalt give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it; for he is poor, and setteth his heart upon it: lest he cry against thee unto the LORD, and it be sin unto thee.

modern.text: You are to pay his wages each day before sunset, because he is poor and depends on them. Otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.

original.text: בְּיוֹמוֹ֩ תִתֵּ֨ן שְׂכָר֜וֹ וְֽלֹא תָב֧וֹא עָלָ֣יו הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֤י עָנִי֙ ה֔וּא וְאֵלָ֕יו ה֥וּא נֹשֵׂ֖א אֶת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא יִקְרָ֤א עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל יְהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה בְךָ֖ חֵֽטְא

verses.restored: Fathers shall not be put to death for children, and children shall not be put to death for fathers; each man shall be put to death for his own sin/misalignment.

familiar.text: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin.

modern.text: Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.

original.text: לֹֽא יוּמְת֤וּ אָבוֹת֙ עַל בָּנִ֔ים וּבָנִ֖ים לֹא יוּמְת֣וּ עַל אָב֑וֹת אִ֥יש בְּחֶטְא֖וֹ יוּמָֽתוּ

verses.restored: You shall not bend judgment of sojourner or orphan, and you shall not take garment of widow as pledge.

familiar.text: Thou shalt not pervert the judgment of the stranger, nor of the fatherless; nor take a widow’s raiment to pledge:

modern.text: Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow’s cloak as security.

original.text: לֹ֣א תַטֶּ֔ה מִשְׁפַּ֖ט גֵּ֣ר יָת֑וֹם וְלֹ֣א תַחֲבֹ֔ל בֶּ֖גֶד אַלְמָנָֽה

verses.restored: You shall remember you were a slave in Egypt and YHWH your Divine redeemed you from there; therefore I command you to do this thing.

familiar.text: But thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt, and the LORD thy God redeemed thee thence: therefore I command thee to do this thing.

modern.text: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from that place. Therefore I am commanding you to do this.

original.text: וְזָכַרְתָּ֗ כִּ֣י עֶ֤בֶד הָיִ֨יתָ֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וַֽיִּפְדְּךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מִשָּׁ֑ם עַל כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת אֶת הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: When you reap your harvest in field and forget a sheaf in field, you shall not return to take it; it shall be for sojourner, orphan, and widow, so YHWH your Divine may bless you in all work of your hands.

familiar.text: When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that the LORD thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hands.

modern.text: If you are harvesting in your field and forget a sheaf there, do not go back to get it. It is to be left for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

original.text: כִּ֣י תִקְצֹר֩ קְצִֽירְךָ֨ בְשָׂדֶ֜ךָ וְשָֽׁכַחְתָּ֧ עֹ֣מֶר בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה לֹ֤א תָשׁוּב֙ לְקַחְתּ֔וֹ לַגֵּ֛ר לַיָּת֥וֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֑ה לְמַ֤עַן יְבָרֶכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכֹ֖ל מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over branches after yourself; it shall be for sojourner, orphan, and widow.

familiar.text: When thou beatest thine olive tree, thou shalt not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.

modern.text: When you beat the olives from your trees, you must not go over the branches again. What remains will be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.

original.text: כִּ֤י תַחְבֹּט֙ זֵֽיתְךָ֔ לֹ֥א תְפָאֵ֖ר אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ לַגֵּ֛ר לַיָּת֥וֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָ֖ה יִהְיֶֽה

verses.restored: When you gather grapes of your vineyard, you shall not glean after yourself; it shall be for sojourner, orphan, and widow.

familiar.text: When thou gatherest the grapes of thy vineyard, thou shalt not glean it afterward: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.

modern.text: When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you must not go over the vines again. What remains will be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.

original.text: כִּ֤י תִבְצֹר֙ כַּרְמְךָ֔ לֹ֥א תְעוֹלֵ֖ל אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ לַגֵּ֛ר לַיָּת֥וֹם וְלָאַלְמָנָ֖ה יִהְיֶֽה

verses.restored: You shall remember you were a slave in land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.

familiar.text: And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt: therefore I command thee to do this thing.

modern.text: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. Therefore I am commanding you to do this.

original.text: וְזָ֣כַרְתָּ֔ כִּי עֶ֥בֶד הָיִ֖יתָ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם עַל כֵּ֞ן אָנֹכִ֤י מְצַוְּךָ֙ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת אֶת הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה

translation_notes: The divorce law assumes male-initiated divorce and gives the woman a written document, but it does not establish equal marital agency. The phrase ervat davar is debated and should not be converted into unrestricted fault-finding.
The remarriage prohibition regulates the first husband's claim after a subsequent marriage; it must not stigmatize divorced or remarried people.
The newlywed exemption protects time for a new household and obligates the husband to bring joy to his wife.
Taking a millstone is forbidden because it seizes the debtor's means of making food and therefore takes life as collateral.
Kidnapping a person for exploitation or sale is condemned, though broader slavery remains elsewhere in the legal corpus.
Scale-disease language is ritual/medical tradition and must not stigmatize skin conditions or blame illness on wrongdoing.
Same-day wages recognize that workers' lives depend upon prompt payment.
Individual-liability law rejects execution of relatives for another person's offense.
Gleaning deliberately leaves productive value in field, olive tree, and vineyard for immigrant, orphan, and widow.
safety_note: Do not use Deuteronomy 24 to shame divorced people, trap anyone in unsafe marriage, exploit workers, seize essential household tools, kidnap or traffic people, stigmatize illness, punish families for another person's conduct, or deny immigrants and widows justice. Center prompt wages, protected collateral, individual responsibility, and food left deliberately for vulnerable neighbors.
